вопрос: What are the symptoms of Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia?
эталон (ответ из датасета): Signs and symptoms of chronic myelogenous leukemia include fever, night sweats, and tiredness. These and other signs and symptoms may be caused by CML or by other conditions. Check with your doctor if you have any of the following: - Feeling very tired. - Weight loss for no known reason. - Night sweats. - Fever. - Pain or a feeling of fullness below the ribs on the left side. Sometimes CML does not cause any symptoms at all.
LingSante: ответ: Many people with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) have no noticeable signs early on, and it’s often found during routine blood tests. When symptoms occur, they may include fatigue, unexplained weight loss, fever, night sweats, easy bruising or bleeding, and a feeling of fullness or discomfort under the ribs due to an enlarged spleen. Some people also notice frequent infections or anemia-related weakness. If you have persistent concerning symptoms, it’s best to discuss them with your healthcare provider for proper evaluation.

* Night sweats
* Unexplained weight loss

Many people with CML have no symptoms at all, which is why regular check-ups are important. If you notice any persistent changes in your health, consult your doctor for proper evaluation and guidance.

вопрос: What are the treatments for Kawasaki syndrome?
эталон (ответ из датасета): How might Kawasaki disease be treated? Intravenous gamma globulin is the standard treatment for Kawasaki disease and is administered in high doses. Children with Kawasaki disease usually greatly improve within 24 hours of treatment with IV gamma globulin. Aspirin is often given in combination with the IV gamma globulin as part of the treatment plan. We found limited information on the management of Kawasaki disease specifically in adults, however you may find the following articles to be helpful: Dauphin C. et al., Kawasaki disease is also a disease of adults: report of six cases. Arch Mal Coeur Vaiss [serial online]. 2007;100(5):439-447. Sve P, Stankovic K, Smail A, Durand DV, Marchand G, and Broussolle C. Adult Kawasaki disease: report of two cases and literature review. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2005;34(6):785-792. Sve P, Bui-Xuan C, Charhon A, and Broussolle C. Adult Kawasaki disease. Rev Med Interne [serial online]. 2003;24(9):577-584.In the article listed above by Dauphin C. et al. the authors describe that of the five adult patients with Kawasaki disease who were treated, all progressed favorably after a course of immunoglobulins. In addition, in the article by Sve P. et al., the authors comment that 'although adult KD often was diagnosed after the acute phase, when a significant beneficial effect from gammaglobulin infusion could not be expected, this treatment did appear to shorten the course of the disease.'
LingSante: ответ: Treatment for Kawasaki disease focuses on reducing inflammation and preventing coronary artery complications. Standard care includes high-dose aspirin initially, followed by low-dose aspirin, plus a single infusion of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) given within the first 10 days of illness. If fever persists despite IVIG, additional therapies such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants may be considered under specialist guidance. Long-term follow-up with echocardiograms is essential to monitor heart involvement and guide further therapy if needed.
LingSante + RAG: ответ: Kawasaki disease is typically treated with intravenous immune globulin (IVIG), given as a single infusion, along with high-dose aspirin during the acute phase. This approach reduces fever and inflammation and lowers the risk of coronary artery complications. Children are usually managed in the hospital, especially when heart involvement is suspected. Aspirin is generally used only under medical supervision because of the risk of bleeding and Reye's syndrome. In rare cases where arteries remain affected despite standard therapy, additional medications or procedures may be considered. Always follow the guidance of a pediatric specialist for individualized care.

Егер балада айну, беттің қызылдығы, жеудің беруі сиякты белгілер болса, дереу дәрігерге жүгіну керек.
